chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Ahmad ibn Idris (may God be pleased with him) narrated to us. He said: My father narrated to us. He said: Ibrahim ibn Hashim narrated to us from al-Hasan ibn Mahbub, from Abd al-Aziz ibn al-Abdi, from Abdullah ibn Abi Ya'fur. He said: Abu Abdillah al-Sadiq Ja'far ibn Muhammad (peace be upon him) said:

O Abdullah! When you pray an obligatory prayer, pray it at its time like the prayer of one bidding farewell, who fears he will never return to it again. Then direct your gaze to the place of your prostration, for if you knew who was to your right and to your left, you would perfect your prayer. And know that you are in the presence of One who sees you while you cannot see Him.

key_terms.بين يدي: Literally 'between the hands of,' an Arabic idiom meaning 'in the presence of' or 'before'
key_terms.صلاة فريضة: Obligatory prayer — one of the five daily prayers whose performance is obligatory
key_terms.صلاة مودع: The prayer of one bidding farewell — a metaphor for praying as if it were one's last prayer
key_terms.موضع السجود: The place of prostration — lowering one's gaze symbolizes humility before God

ai.seo_question: What did Imam al-Sadiq say about how to perform obligatory prayer with full presence?
ai.summary: Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq (AS) advises his companion Abdullah ibn Abi Ya'fur on achieving true presence of heart in obligatory prayer. The Imam instructs him to pray each prayer as if it were his last, lower his gaze to the prostration spot, and remain conscious that unseen spiritual beings are present on both sides. This teaching was addressed directly to one of the Imam's most trusted companions and reflects the Shia emphasis on quality of prayer over mere formal observance.
word_analysis: the hands of (i.e. in front of)

en.bilal-muhammad: Al-Husayn b. Ahmad b. Idris (ra) narrated to us. He said: My father narrated to us. He said: Ibrahim b. Hashim narrated to us from al-Hasan b. Mahbub from `Abd al-`Aziz b. al-`Abdi from `Abdullah b. Abi Ya`fur.  He said: Abu `Abdillah al-Sadiq Ja`far b. Muhammad (as) said:

O `Abdullah! When you pray an obligatory prayer, then pray it on-time in a meek way, fearing that you will never return to it again. Look to the place of your prostration (humble your sight), for if you knew who was to your right and to your left, you would have perfected your prayer. Know that you are before He who sees you while you cannot see Him.
